hero.oneLiner: One of India's leading electrical and electronics (E&E) companies, among the top two players in wiring harnesses for two-wheelers and three-wheelers in India with a leadership position in EV 2W/3W wiring harnesses.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: One of India's leading electrical and electronics (E&E) companies, among the top two players in wiring harnesses for two-wheelers and three-wheelers in India with a leadership position in EV 2W/3W wiring harnesses.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Dhoot Transmission designs, engineers, manufactures and supplies critical wiring harnesses that integrate electronic sensors and controllers, switches, terminals, connectors, junction boxes, high-voltage interconnection systems and data cables, for both ICE and EV platforms. Its product lines are wiring harnesses, battery packs, sensors and electronic controllers, and automotive switches, sold mainly to 2W and 3W OEMs in India with a diversified presence extending into commercial vehicles, off-highway vehicles, and farming/industrial equipment.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Dhoot Automotive Systems Private Limited (DASPL) — Material Subsidiary: Identified as material per Regulation 16(1)(c) of SEBI Listing Regulations; party to Net Proceeds debt repayment, RVL JV master framework agreement (67% DASPL / 33% RVL) and Multilink business transfer
- Dhoot Autocomponents Private Limited (DACPL) — Material Subsidiary: Party to Net Proceeds debt repayment
- Dhoot Electricals Systems Private Limited (DESPL) — Material Subsidiary: Party to Net Proceeds debt repayment
- Dhoot Transmission UK Limited — Foreign Subsidiary: Party to Net Proceeds debt repayment
- Dhoot Electrical Solutions Private Limited (DWSPL, formerly Dhoot Wirings Systems Pvt Ltd) — Subsidiary: Entered Merger Framework Agreement dated February 18, 2026 to merge FourFront Limited into DWSPL
- Mangalam Capital Private Limited (formerly Mangalam Coils Private Limited) — Group Company / Promoter Group entity: Promoter Group Selling Shareholder in the Offer for Sale
- Dhoot Holdings Private Limited (DHPL) and downstream entities — Direct Subsidiary: Acquired during 9M ended Dec-2025 in a common-control business combination; Restated Consolidated Financial Information for FY23-FY25 restated as if combination occurred from April 1, 2022 (Ind AS 103 Appendix C)

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Wiring Harnesses:** ICE wiring harnesses, EV wiring harnesses / electrical distribution systems, high-voltage interconnection systems, auxiliary wiring harnesses, co-axial cables, data cables
- **Battery Packs:** EV battery packs
- **Sensors & Electronic Controllers:** ABS sensors, lean angle sensors, rollover sensors, wheel speed sensors, USB chargers, light control modules, dock chargers, side stand sensors (in development), temperature sensors (in development)
- **Automotive Switches:** keypad switches, rocker switches
- **Others:** auto components, moulds and dies, scrap and other materials

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- 2W - two-wheelers (66.91% of revenue from operations, FY2025)
- 3W - three-wheelers (12.50% of revenue from operations, FY2025)
- Others - commercial vehicles (CV), off-highway vehicles (OHW), farming and industrial equipment (20.59% of revenue from operations, FY2025)

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward integrated in critical wiring-harness components — terminals, connectors, cables and moulded parts — manufactured in-house to lower procurement overhead, secure supply against external disruption, and enable in-line quality control. Principal raw materials are copper, brass and polymers plus connectors, terminals, cables, mouldings (incl. rubber) and electronic components (sensors, PCBs); sourced domestically (principally Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Haryana) and internationally (China, Switzerland, Germany). All suppliers are required to be IATF-certified. Company strategy also includes forward moves into power electronics/charging sub-systems (DC-DC converters, on-board chargers, BJB sub-systems) and expansion of EV battery-pack interconnect systems from a single- to a multi-customer model.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- EBITDA margin expansion from 14.05% (FY2023) to 18.31% (FY2024) to 17.15% (FY2025), aided by revenue growth and mix shift, though margin dipped FY24-to-FY25
- PAT margin trajectory: 7.69% (FY2023) to 10.67% (FY2024) to 10.19% (FY2025)
- Product-mix shift toward EV: EV revenue as % of total revenue from operations rose from 8.05% (FY2023) to 16.19% (FY2024) to 25.22% (FY2025), moderating slightly to 24.78% in 9M ended Dec-2025
- Rising net capital expenditure intensity: 6.41% of revenue (FY2023) to 9.73% (FY2024) to 11.17% (FY2025) to 7.79% (9M Dec-2025), reflecting the ongoing capacity build-out
- Leverage trending up: net debt to EBITDA of 1.25x (FY2023), 0.99x (FY2024), 1.29x (FY2025) and 1.51x (9M Dec-2025)
- High and rising customer concentration: top-5-customer revenue share of 64.67% (FY2023) to 66.17% (FY2024) to 71.18% (FY2025) to 72.49% (9M Dec-2025)
- Return ratios declining off a high base: RoCE fell from 33.56% (FY2024) to 29.66% (FY2025) to 22.34% (9M Dec-2025, annualised basis not stated); RoE fell from 39.88% (FY2024) to 35.60% (FY2025) to 23.03% (9M Dec-2025)
- Working-capital and margin levers include VAVE (value analysis/value engineering) and localisation initiatives with OEM customers that reduce prices while protecting margins

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Capitalise on electrification and premiumisation trends to broaden the product portfolio: expand wiring harnesses into off-highway/commercial vehicle segments, increase harness content per platform (auxiliary harnesses, co-axial cables, data cables), scale EV battery pack interconnect systems from a single-customer to multi-customer model, and expand into power electronics/charging sub-systems (DC-DC converters, on-board chargers, BJB sub-systems) targeting CV segment
- Continue investment in design, R&D and engineering capabilities, including a planned state-of-the-art R&D centre with integrated design, engineering, advanced testing and validation capabilities, to be funded through internal accruals and sanctioned term loans
- Invest ahead of demand through capacity expansion - co-locating capacity near customer sites and modularising/scaling capacity in line with confirmed customer orders; adding new facilities at Hosur (Tamil Nadu, wiring harnesses) and Chakan, Pune (battery manufacturing), both expected to become operational in 2026
- Pursue selective inorganic growth (acquisitions, joint ventures, technology partnerships) in Europe and Asia to access new technologies, customers and markets, with disciplined capital allocation, Board-level oversight and defined ROCE targets; recent examples include the DASPL-Ride Vision Limited (RVL) ADAS joint venture (67%/33%) and the DWSPL-FourFront Limited merger framework agreement

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The company is funding two new wiring-harness-adjacent plants from IPO Net Proceeds: the Jhajjar Wiring Harness Plant (Haryana, ~5.13 acres, total cost Rs.847.91 million, commissioning by May 2027) and the Hosur Wiring Harness Plant (Tamil Nadu, 7.28 acres leased for 99 years, total cost Rs.1,406.09 million, commissioning around May 2027 per the detailed schedule, though the Risk Factors section separately describes this Hosur facility as expected to complete by Q2 FY2027). It is also constructing a battery-pack assembly facility at Chakan, Pune, expected to complete by Q1 FY2027, and states it has four under-construction plants in India in total as of the UDRHP-I date (approvals pending/being applied for). Beyond these projects, management plans a new R&D/testing centre (cost and timeline undisclosed, to be funded via internal accruals and term loans) and continued inorganic expansion in Europe and Asia.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Established leadership position in India's 2W/3W wiring harness market: 44.64% value share in 2W+3W combined (Top 2), more than 70% share in electric 2W/3W (Leader), FY2025 (Source: CRISIL Report)
- Backward integration in critical components (terminals, connectors, cables, moulded parts) lowers costs, secures supply and improves quality control
- Marquee, diversified OEM customer base with long-standing relationships (average relationship with top five customers of 13 years as of Dec-2025); top 5 customers combined 2W market share of 66.24% of the Indian 2W market
- Track record of strong and improving financial performance: PAT CAGR of 46.94% (FY2023-FY2025), EBITDA margin up from 14.05% to 17.15% over the same period
- Professional, experienced management team and Board (MD with 27+ years' experience; Chairman with 38+ years in the automotive sector) plus strategic sponsorship and governance support from Bain Capital-affiliated promoter BC Asia XV
- Architecture-agnostic product portfolio (~95% of auto product portfolio is EV-focused or powertrain-neutral) positioning the company across ICE, hybrid and BEV platforms
- In-house R&D/engineering organisation (232 design/engineering/R&D staff as of Dec-2025, 8.65% of total staff) enabling rapid new product development (e.g., USB Type-C charger developed and industrialised within four months for a leading 2W OEM)

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Sector and product concentration — 66.91% of FY2025 revenue from operations came from the 2W automotive sector and 12.50% from 3W, with wiring harnesses alone comprising 78.00% of FY2025 revenue - any downturn in 2W/3W demand or wiring-harness pricing/technology directly hits the business
- Customer concentration — Top customer Bajaj Auto contributed 35.08% of FY2025 revenue (32.33% in 9M Dec-2025); top 5 customers contributed 71.18% of FY2025 revenue (72.49% in 9M Dec-2025) and top 10 customers 81.81% - loss of any major OEM relationship would be materially adverse
- Execution risk on under-construction facilities — Hosur (wiring harness) and Chakan, Pune (battery pack assembly) facilities are under construction with expected completion in Q2 and Q1 FY2027 respectively (per Risk Factors); company flags possible delays/cost overruns from regulatory approvals and construction delays
- Elevated tax litigation exposure — 26 tax proceedings pending against the Company and 2 against Subsidiaries as of the UDRHP-I date, with aggregate amount involved of approx Rs.234 million (Company) and Rs.2.81 million (Subsidiaries); materiality threshold for civil litigation is Rs.136.09 million
- Historical corporate-record gaps and a compliance instance — Company was unable to locate certain historical RoC records (Form 18/challan for a 2007 registered-office change) and relied on an independent search report; DRHP also flags an instance of certain non-compliances under the Companies Act in the past
- Rising leverage alongside capex intensity — Net debt to EBITDA rose to 1.51x (9M Dec-2025) from 0.99x (FY2024), while net capex ran at 11.17% of revenue in FY2025, as the company funds new plants partly through debt
- Recent promoter/ownership transition and business combination — BC Asia XV (Bain Capital) acquired a 49% stake in April 2025 (now 55% pre-Offer) and the Company completed a common-control acquisition of Dhoot Holdings Private Limited and downstream entities during 9M ended Dec-2025, requiring restatement of FY2023-FY2025 financials as if combined from April 1, 2022
